## Audit conclusion

H04 was accepted under the recorded Selection rule, and two supplied subsequent student builds demonstrably implemented numerical projection checks. In the bunk-room example, executed output confirms the camera-aim sign and restoration; in the classroom example, it confirms a trial and a revised camera. These are **specific observed uses of prompted guidance**, not proof of a generally learned reconstruction capability or of visually accurate final scenes.

**Scope.** This is a text-only audit of the supplied extracts and complete files, not an inspection of the referenced images or unprovided experiments. The two trajectories are truncated; the final-build files and separate logs supply additional evidence, but do not make their omitted trajectory events audited. Teacher and student visual assessments below remain claims. Numerical projections establish where chosen 3D points project, not whether the points correspond correctly, are visible, or trace the rendered silhouette.

## Proposal and acceptance

The teacher reported that three development scenes ran and passed structural checks despite substantial framing errors: a bedroom window and chair, a restaurant pendant and depth-dependent anchor errors, and kitchen counter/hob displacement. The teacher also reported incorrect predictions about raising camera aim and unreliable bounds crossing the camera plane. Those scene-specific diagnoses are not independently verifiable from the supplied later classroom and bunk-room records. The general sign issue is supported by the later numerical bunk-room trial, but that does not independently validate the teacher’s earlier trajectory diagnosis. [Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/meta_traces/round04/decisions.json`, first object, `analysis`.]

The targeted change was H-only: add a small explicit-landmark projection check, before/after camera trials, original-aspect handling, and a warning that projection is not visibility or appearance verification. It did not introduce a material, connectivity, or reusable M action. [Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/candidates/C04/H/policy.py`, lines 6–35 and 52–55; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/candidates/C04/H.diff`.]

The round record reports three scheduled, completed and evaluated Selection cases, eligibility, `S_BW=37.89522977022977`, `Q=0.3520422890476687`, and a frozen BW gain of `3.205544455544455`. H04 was retained from H02; M remained M000, with no M candidate or actions. This is acceptance under **absolute eligibility then frozen BW gain**, not a direct test that every defect was repaired, nor evidence of weight training or durable internal learning. The record says the changed module was executed or its entry used; the student artifacts below are the stronger evidence of particular adoption. [Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/rounds/04/record.json`, keys `selection`, `reason`, `H_accepted`, `M_accepted`, `H_retained`, `M_retained`, `action_count`; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/candidates/C04/worker_summary.json`, `actions`.]

## Actual student evidence and concern-by-concern findings

### Camera, framing, position and orientation

**Bunk room.** The first executed build printed separate reference estimates and projections: for example, column foot `(0.72, 0.84)` versus `(0.66, 0.668)`, and rear panel upper-left `(0.77, 0.34)` versus `(0.617, 0.429)`. The first build and render completed with return code zero; that verifies execution, not reconstruction quality. [Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/trajectory.jsonl`, events 3–4 and 6–9.]

The second-step log shows a lens trial’s tradeoff: the column foot moved from `(0.669, 0.695)` to `(0.761, 0.802)`, while the foreground bench point moved from `(0.116, 0.7)` to `(-0.094, 0.81)`. The final build then actually implements a retained-camera, upward-aim trial and restoration. Its executed log shows all six chosen points moving downward in image coordinates: e.g. column foot `y=.802` to `.816`, then back to `.802`; the restored table matches the retained table. This directly supports the sign for that trial, not the visibility or correctness of each correspondence. The recorded final camera is perspective, 48 mm, 384×512, and selection names step 3. [Sources: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/steps/002/build_stdout.log`, lines 3–5; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/steps/003/build_stdout.log`, lines 3–23; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/camera.json`, keys `lens`, `type`, `width`, `height`; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/selected.json`, `step`.]

The student’s final comments report inconsistent foreground/background errors, retain the camera, and propose local corrections to the wall fixtures, column, bunk, lockers and lamp. The code contains corresponding geometry and position choices, so these are more than claims of intent; however, the supplied text does not independently verify their final visual effect. [Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/build.py`, lines 1–30 and 55–76.]

**Classroom.** The student also adopted the projection method: the executed step-2 log compares previous, small downward-trial and revised aim; board upper-left `y` moves `.476 → .464 → .380`. Step 3 tests aim and lens together, then records a revised camera: the selected window point moves from `(.152,.285)` to `(.089,.223)` against the student’s estimated `(.04,.18)`. Because aim and lens both change in the small step-3 trial, that trial alone cannot isolate their individual effects. The final camera file records 27 mm at 512×340 and selection records step 3. These are computed point improvements relative to uncertain student estimates, not verified visible-contour improvements. [Sources: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_104864364/1/steps/002/build_stdout.log`, lines 3–20; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_104864364/1/steps/003/build_stdout.log`, lines 3–20; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_104864364/1/camera.json`, keys `lens`, `width`, `height`; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_104864364/1/selected.json`, `step`.]

### Multi-object coverage and disconnected parts

The teacher’s proposal concerns framing of multiple scene anchors, not a diagnosis that objects were missing or physically disconnected. H04’s projection addition is therefore **indirectly relevant to coverage within the frame**, but is not a connectivity repair. Existing system guidance in the student request already called for inventories, separate assets, overlaps and gaps; those instructions themselves are not adoption evidence. [Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/trajectory.jsonl`, event 1.]

Actual code constructs a multi-object bunk room with architecture, bunk components, lockers, benches and fixtures, and a classroom with repeated desk/bench assemblies, bags, windows and fans. The classroom student claims the prior bench supports were overly solid and implements thin legs; the bunk-room student claims fixtures were cropped and places them on a wall return. These are implemented design choices, not verification that all reference objects are present or correctly connected. Separate meshes and asset membership alone neither prove an erroneous disconnection nor prove physical contact. No supplied numerical contact test establishes either defect or repair. [Sources: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/build.py`, lines 1–30 and 79–120; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_104864364/1/build.py`, lines 1–27 and the `student_station` function.]

### Material, texture, lighting and rendering

The teacher did not diagnose a specific material or texture defect in the round-04 proposal; the new projection check explicitly cannot establish material appearance. The bunk-room student claims the previous floor was too light and uniform and implements darker floor color and reduced world/light strengths. The classroom student claims a flatter floor and calls for warm tile variation; the supplied final code implements floor joints and a base color, but does not establish a faithful varied texture. Neither claim can be visually verified here, and illumination, material and surface orientation are confounded. [Sources: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_118588033/1/build.py`, lines 15–29 and world/light setup; `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_104864364/1/build.py`, lines 14–27 and `Floor tile joints`.]

Both supplied trajectory excerpts record successful first builds and renders, not visual success. The classroom’s first execution reports `ok=true`; its initial window point projected `(.158,.383)` against estimated `(.04,.18)`, illustrating that technical success can coexist with substantial point mismatch. No technical failure is established in these reviewed excerpts; the policy’s failure-handling instructions are not evidence that a failure occurred. The system text describes a smaller budget than the actual initial request, which reports four model calls, three executions and about 3,600 seconds; this discrepancy limits reliance on the generic budget description. [Source: `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H04/development/commons_104864364/1/trajectory.jsonl`, events 1 and 6–8.]

**Bottom line:** the records verify a targeted policy change, rule-based acceptance, and concrete projection-check adoption in two later builds. They do not verify final visual fidelity, complete object coverage, material quality, connectivity, or generalization beyond the reviewed evidence.
